title: My Hens Quit Laying This Week. It Wasn't the Cold — Here's What It Was
description:
My twelve hens went from nine eggs a day to two in one week. Everybody said it was the cold. It wasn't. Here's what it really was, the seven things I check in order (five of them free), what it cost me, and what my red hen Dottie was hiding in the barn.

What I check when the eggs drop off, cheapest first:
1. Daylight — hens need about 14 hours of light to lay steady; under 12 they slow way down.
2. The molt — feathers on the floor, pin feathers, bright eyes and eating = molt, not sickness.
3. The feed tag — molting hens need more protein: I switch from 16% layer to an 18-20% all-flock feed, with oyster shell on the side. Less scratch.
4. Missing eggs — look for egg eating and hidden nests (check the barn!).
5. Mites — wipe a white paper towel under the roost after dark.
6. Stress — tracks, digging, feathers outside the fence.
7. Age — a hen lays the most in her first two years.

What I won't buy: egg laying boosters, heat lamps, fancy molting formulas, lights left on all night.

pinned_comment:
Quick answer for anybody in a hurry: in the fall it's usually the LIGHT (under 12 hours) plus the MOLT. Switch to an 18-20% all-flock feed with oyster shell on the side, cut back the scratch, and check the barn for a hidden nest before you buy anything. 🐔
